body.statement:
Let \(\{I_\gamma:\gamma\in\mathcal G\}\) be a finite family of Bernoulli random variables, let \(B_\gamma\subseteq\mathcal G\) be dependency neighborhoods such that \(I_\gamma\) is independent of \(\{I_\zeta:\zeta\notin B_\gamma\}\), and put
\[
 W=\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal G}I_\gamma,\qquad
 \mu=\mathbb EW,qquad
 b_1=\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal G}\sum_{\zeta\in B_\gamma}
       \mathbb EI_\gamma\,\mathbb EI_\zeta,qquad
 b_2=\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal G}\sum_{\substack{\zeta\in B_\gamma\\\zeta\ne\gamma}}
       \mathbb E(I_\gamma I_\zeta).
\]
Then, for total variation defined as the supremum over measurable events,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(\mathcal L(W),\operatorname{Poisson}(\mu)\right)
 \le 2(b_1+b_2).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 1, first total-variation bound, specialized to dependency neighborhoods with the supremum-over-events convention
source.verbatim_statement: THEOREM 1. Let W be the number of occurrences of dependent events, and let Z be a Poisson random variable with EZ = EW = λ. Then ‖ℒ(W) − ℒ(Z)‖ ≤ 2[(b₁ + b₂)(1 − e^(−λ))/λ + b₃(1 ∧ 1.4λ^(−1/2))] ≤ 2(b₁ + b₂ + b₃), and |P(W = 0) − e^(−λ)| ≤ (b₁ + b₂ + b₃)(1 − e^(−λ))/λ < (1 ∧ λ^(−1))(b₁ + b₂ + b₃).

upstream.citation: Chen, L. H. Y. (1975), Poisson approximation for dependent trials
upstream.locator: AGG p. 10 states Theorem 1 is essentially contained in Chen (1975)

attestation.note: Transcribed from Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989), printed p. 11, Theorem 1; the graph node uses the weaker b3=0 consequence after converting their norm, defined as twice the supremum-over-events distance, to this project convention.
